questions.question: Compare sandstone and shale.
questions.expected_answer: Sandstone is made of sand grains glued together, so it feels rough and gritty, you can see the grains, and it is often cream, yellow, brown or red with stripes of layers. Shale is made of mud of very fine silt and clay, so it feels smooth, its grains cannot be seen, it is often grey or black, and it splits easily into thin, flat sheets along its layers.

questions.question: How does limestone form, and how can you test for it?
questions.expected_answer: Most limestone formed in warm, shallow seas, where the shells and skeletons of sea creatures piled up on the sea floor, were broken up, and over millions of years were squashed and hardened into rock. To test for limestone, drip vinegar on it: limestone fizzes, giving off bubbles of carbon dioxide, while sandstone and shale usually do not.

questions.question: Describe one use each of limestone, sandstone and shale.
questions.expected_answer: Limestone is crushed, mixed with clay and heated in a kiln to make cement, which is used in concrete; it is also used as agricultural lime. Sandstone is cut into blocks for buildings, like the Union Buildings in Pretoria, and used for paving and walls. Shale is crushed, shaped and fired to make bricks and roof tiles, and slabs are used for paving.
